# PhysicsHub

> Free, open-source educational platform featuring interactive physics simulations and theoretical guides for students, educators, and developers.

## Overview

PhysicsHub provides real-time browser-based physics visualizations covering kinematics, dynamics, harmonic motion, vectors, collision theory, and modern physics. Each simulation provides interactive controls, mathematical formulations, and visual representations to help students understand abstract physical concepts.

- Website: https://physicshub.github.io
- Repository: https://github.com/physicshub/physicshub.github.io
- License: Open Source (MIT)

## Interactive Simulations

- [Bouncing Ball](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/BouncingBall): Simulation of the ball bouncing off the walls. A playful first look at motion, speed and collisions — suited for middle school and even younger explorers.
- [Vector Operations Calculator](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/VectorsOperations): Interactive 2D vector calculator — visualize addition, subtraction, and dot products in real time. The standard high-school tool for students learning vector physics.
- [Ball Acceleration](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/BallAcceleration): Simulate a ball accelerating toward your cursor in real time. Explore velocity and uniform acceleration, a core topic from middle-school physics onward — free online.
- [Ball Gravity](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/BallGravity): Watch a ball fall and bounce under gravity and external forces in real time. Adjust mass, elasticity, and gravitational force to explore Newton's laws — free interactive simulation for high-school physics.
- [Spring Mass System Simulator](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/SpringConnection): Explore Hooke's Law and Simple Harmonic Motion interactively. Adjust mass and spring constant to visualize oscillations and energy conservation — an extended high-school (A-Level) topic.
- [Simple Pendulum Simulation](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/SimplePendulum): Simulate a pendulum and calculate its period and frequency in real time. Explore how length, gravity, and energy are related, in a standard high-school topic — free interactive physics tool.
- [Projectile & Parabolic Motion](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/ParabolicMotion): Simulate projectile motion and predict trajectory, range, and max height instantly. A staple of high-school kinematics — interactive parabolic motion calculator, free online.
- [Inclined Plane](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/InclinedPlane): Simulate a block sliding down an inclined plane with friction. Adjust angle, mass, and surface to explore forces and Newton's laws — a core high-school dynamics experiment.
- [Circular Motion](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/CircularMotion): Simulate uniform circular motion in real time. Visualize velocity and centripetal acceleration vectors while adjusting radius and speed — an extended high-school to first-year university topic.
- [Three Body Problem](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/ThreeBody): Simulate a classic physics problem of three bodies operating under the gravity of each other. A numerically advanced topic aimed at university level (and keen high-school students).
- [Horizontal Spring](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/HorizontalSpring): A spring attached to the left wall with a draggable mass. Explore Hooke's Law and oscillation on a horizontal plane — approachable from middle school, standard in high school.
- [Double Pendulum](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/DoublePendulum): Simulate a double pendulum and explore chaotic motion. Watch how small changes in initial conditions lead to completely different trajectories — a classic university-level example of chaos theory.
- [1D Collision simulation](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/CollisionSimulation): Simulate 1D elastic collisions with velocity vectors, momentum, and kinetic energy visualization — a core momentum topic in high-school physics.
- [Pi From Collisions](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/PiCollisions): Simulate two colliding blocks of different masses to derive pi. A beautiful conservation-law puzzle for university students (and gifted high-schoolers): adjust the mass of the larger block by a power of 100 to see further precision of pi.
- [Trigonometric Circle](https://physicshub.github.io/simulations/TrigonometricCircle): Interactive unit circle with a draggable angle θ. Visualize sin, cos, tan, cot, sec and csc as circle segments, watch the generalized wave A·sin(ωθ+φ) plot in real time, and trace the inverse functions arcsin, arccos, arctan and arccot — a bridge from middle-school geometry to high-school trig.

## Educational Guides & Theory

- [What Is Physics? A Visual, Interactive Introduction for Beginners](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/what-is-physics): Physics explained visually — not just with formulas. Discover the major branches of physics, real-world applications, and explore free interactive simulations to see the science in action.
- [Class 12 Physics Complete Guide – All Chapters with Formulas & Examples](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/class-12-physics-complete-guide): Master Class 12 Physics (CBSE 2025–26) with clear explanations, key formulas, derivations, and solved examples — Electrostatics, Magnetism, Optics, Modern Physics and more.
- [Physics of Bouncing Balls: How a Bouncing Ball Works](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/physics-bouncing-ball-comprehensive-educational-guide): Explore the physics of a bouncing ball: from kinematic equations to energy dissipation. Learn about gravity, restitution, and Newton's laws with our interactive JS simulator.
- [Vectors: components, addition, dot and cross products](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/comprehensive-guide-to-vector-operations): A vector carries a magnitude and a direction. Split it into components and the algebra falls out: addition, scaling, the dot product for angles, the cross product for area and torque.
- [How does a ball accelerate toward a target?](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/ball-uniformly-accelerated-motion): Acceleration is how fast velocity changes. Point a constant acceleration at a target and the ball speeds up, overshoots, then loops back — here is why, with a simulation to try.
- [Free Fall & Air Resistance: Interactive Physics Simulation Guide](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/ball-free-fall-comprehensive-guide): Explore how gravity, air resistance, and wind affect a falling ball. Interactive simulations and clear explanations covering free fall, drag force, and planetary gravity — from beginner to advanced.
- [How does a spring work?](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/spring-connection): A spring pushes back in proportion to how far you stretch it — that is Hooke's law, and it is exactly what makes a mass on a spring oscillate. Here is the physics, with a simulation.
- [The Physics of the Pendulum: This is How It Works](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/physics-of-pendulum-explained): An exhaustive exploration of pendulum dynamics from elementary observations to advanced nonlinear analysis, encompassing simple harmonic motion, energy conservation, chaotic behavior, and quantum mechanical interpretations.
- [How does projectile motion work?](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/projectile-parabolic-motion): Gravity pulls a projectile straight down while its sideways speed stays constant. Those two independent motions combine into a parabola — here is the maths, with an interactive launcher.
- [The Three-Body Problem: The Equation That Broke Physics](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/physics-behind-three-body-problem): Two bodies orbiting under gravity are perfectly predictable; three are chaotic. Why the three-body problem has no formula — and what the Netflix show gets right and wrong.
- [How Two Sliding Blocks Compute π — The Most Surprising Result in Physics](https://physicshub.github.io/blog/pi-from-block-collisions-explained): Two frictionless blocks and a wall, all collisions elastic: count the clacks and you get the digits of π. The physics behind it, from the first collision to the geometric proof.

## Core Topics & Disciplines

- **Kinematics & Motion**: Displacement, velocity, uniform acceleration, parabolic trajectories.
- **Classical Dynamics**: Newton's laws of motion, gravitational fields, air resistance, elastic & inelastic collisions.
- **Harmonic Oscillations**: Simple harmonic motion (SHM), Hooke's law, spring-mass systems, pendulums.
- **Mathematical Tools**: Vector arithmetic, 2D vector decomposition, dot products, trigonometry.

## Optional & Deep Resources

- [Full Knowledge Base](https://physicshub.github.io/llms-full.txt): Detailed simulation parameters, formulas, target educational levels, and complete documentation.
